subject: Renewal: MerchantLane - rate guard, commit redline and burst plan
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@merchantlane.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal timeline + ask on price guard and burst capacity

Hi Rachel,

Our contract with Redwood is up on Aug 15. We want to move from a pure paygo model to a 12-month committed plan, but we need a short-term price guard through Q4 and a guaranteed burst pool for Black Friday traffic. Priya (cc) will handle procurement/PO. High level asks: 
- 12 month commit that covers historical usage + 25% headroom
- a price hold for 90 days after signature if market rates move up
- temporary burst pool (on-demand) with fixed per-token rate for spikes

Can you share how flexible Redwood is on credits/discount phasing for this? Also, we need a draft SOW to share with legal.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Engineering
MerchantLane
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@merchantlane.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@merchantlane.com>
Date: 2027-07-01T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline + ask on price guard and burst capacity

Sam — thanks for the clear asks. Quick notes before I circulate a formal SOW: 
- We can structure a 12mo committed agreement with a staged discount: higher discount in months 1–4, step down thereafter, or a front-loaded credit pool depending on invoicing preference.
- We can commit to a 90-day market price guard as a contract clause tied to a defined list of covered SKUs; will need legal sign-off for exact language.
- Burst pool: we can allocate a shared burst budget with a capped per-token surcharge; alternatively a reserved burst bucket that auto-bills if used.

I'll attach a draft SOW and a pricing worksheet by EOD tomorrow. Would you prefer credits or an up-front discount?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-02T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MerchantLane renewal - proposed concessions (internal)

Team — forwarding Sam's asks. Proposed response below (highlighted):

Proposed commercial package for approval:
- 12 month commit = 1.25x trailing 12mo runrate (covers headroom)
- Effective blended discount: 18% first 4 months, 10% months 5–12 OR equivalent $500k credit applied front-loaded (customer preference)
- 90-day price guard on generation/embedding SKUs starting at signature (legal to ensure carve-outs for new SKUs)
- Burst pool: 200k tokens/month on-demand at $0.0009/token surcharge; any usage above auto-bills at paygo rates
- One-time onboarding credit of $50k to cover engineering ramp/ops work (applied as invoice credit)

Questions for Neha/legal: does the 90-day guard language need a sunset clause tied to SKU list? Any concerns with the fixed surcharge for burst?

Need approval from Revenue Ops for the $50k credit and from Finance for invoice treatment. If approved, I'll send the SOW + redline and DocuSign link to Sam.

Thanks,
Rachel
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MerchantLane renewal - proposed concessions (internal)

Rachel — quick legal read:
- 90-day price guard is OK provided we enumerate included SKUs and include an explicit carve-out for material new features or large upstream cost changes (e.g., GPU cost pass-through). I'll draft a short clause.
- Burst surcharge is acceptable but add an annualized cap clause so we don't leave open a large exposure if usage is sustained. Suggest cap = 3x committed monthly average for any rolling 30-day period.
- Onboarding credit: mark as contra-revenue, not a discount, and tie it to a milestone (production onboarding). Finance needs to confirm accounting treatment.

I'll attach a legal snippet for inclusion.

—Neha
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@merchantlane.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@merchantlane.com>, Finance Ops <finance@merchantlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-07T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: MerchantLane - formal renewal proposal and redlines attached

Hi Sam / Priya — thanks for the call earlier. Attached are: MerchantLane_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW + pricing worksheet), and redlines_20270707.docx (legal clause draft and price‑guard language). Summary of the commercial: 
- 12mo commit = 1.25x trailing runrate (committed tokens)
- Pricing: blended 18% discount months 1–4, 10% months 5–12 OR $500k front-loaded credit (you pick)
- 90-day price guard on the generation & embedding SKUs with explicit SKU list in appendix; carve-out for new SKUs and upstream pass-throughs
- Burst pool: 200k tokens/month at $0.0009/token surcharge; 30-day sustained cap at 3x committed monthly average (to protect both sides)
- Onboarding credit: $50k conditional on production cutover within 60 days of signature

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm credits vs discount preference and confirm burst size.
2) If agreed, I will send DocuSign and coordinate Finance for PO/invoicing terms.
3) Priya — let me know if you want the SOW as a single consolidated exhibit for legal review.

Attachments referenced as stubs: [MerchantLane_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW, pricing worksheet)], [redlines_20270707.docx (legal clause draft)], [usage_history_Q2.csv]

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jul 09, 2027 at 09:05 AM -07:00, Priya Desai <priya.desai@merchantlane.com> wrote:
From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@merchantlane.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@merchantlane.com>, Finance Ops <finance@merchantlane.com>
Date: 2027-07-09T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantLane - formal renewal proposal and redlines attached

Thanks Rachel — received and reviewed with Finance. A few quick asks before we sign: 
- Can we reduce the onboarding credit milestone from production cutover to completion of security checklist (we own production schedule variability)?
- Burst pool: can you increase to 300k tokens/month but keep the same surcharge? We will tolerate the 30-day cap language.
- For the price guard, can you add a short mutual exit if there is a material change in regulation affecting data residency costs?

If you can accept those three tweaks we'll aim to return a signed DocuSign within 5 business days.

Regards,
Priya Desai
Director, Procurement & Finance
MerchantLane
